items.title: [theglobeandmail.com] B.C. voters cast ballots in close race as officials hand-count votes
items.content_html:
🎨 ✏️

British Columbia voters are choosing a 93-member legislature Saturday in a snap provincial election called two years early, with the governing New Democratic Party (NDP) and the Conservative Party of B.C. running close in final polls. During the campaign, Premier David Eby acknowledged frustration over the early election call, while both major parties promoted competing plans on affordability, health care and the economy. Eby initially cited U.S. President Donald Trump’s trade threat as a reason to seek a new mandate, then said he should have explained more clearly that the legislature had stalled under the NDP’s narrow majority. Eby also accused interim Conservative leader Lorne Doerkson of serving as a “Trojan horse” for extremists in his party; Doerkson called that characterization “absurd”. Election officials will count election-day ballots by hand because the snap vote left Elections BC too little time to prepare enough tabulators. Officials will electronically tabulate advance-voting and electoral-office ballots and report those results first. Absentee and mail-in ballots will not be included in election-night totals; they are scheduled for the final count from Nov. 6 to Nov. 10.

items.title: [latimes.com] Meta faces $25 billion New Mexico penalty as legal costs cut earnings
items.content_html:
🎨 ✏️

Meta reported third-quarter operating income of $13 billion, down 37% from a year earlier, after a $9.9 billion charge for a separate youth-safety settlement. The same day, a New Mexico judge ordered the company to pay $25 billion in a privacy case. Meta’s revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, and the company attributed advertising gains in part to artificial intelligence improvements in engagement and recommendations. The New Mexico order followed a jury’s finding that Meta committed more than 43 million state consumer-protection violations. The judge calculated a potential penalty of more than $219 billion before reducing it to $25 billion. Interest on the award accrues at 15% annually, and the state’s constitution directs consumer-protection penalties to education spending. Meta says it will appeal, a step expected to delay access to the money. Its shares rose 2% in Wednesday afternoon trading, and an analyst quoted by Reuters said the award was unlikely to change the company’s overall value.

items.title: [zmescience.com] Protein evidence identifies Chinese fossils as Denisovans, revealing likely facial traits
items.content_html:
🎨 ✏️

Researchers have identified human fossils from Xujiayao in northern China as Denisovans using ancient proteins, then compared their bones with other remains to infer the group’s likely appearance. The fossils suggest Denisovans had low, backward-sloping foreheads, heavy brow ridges and broad, relatively flat faces, with features distinct from those of Neanderthals. The team recovered a Denisovan-linked collagen variant from two fossils with no surviving DNA. The Xujiayao collection includes 20 specimens excavated decades ago. The researchers argue that some Chinese fossils previously assigned to separate human groups may instead represent variation within the Denisovan lineage. That classification remains uncertain for specimens identified only by resemblance, and researchers say additional samples would help test it.

items._excerpt: Researchers have identified human fossils from Xujiayao in northern China as Denisovans using ancient proteins, then compared their bones with other remains to infer the group’s likely appearance. The fossils suggest Denisovans had low, backward-sloping foreheads, heavy brow ridges and broad, relatively flat faces, with features distinct from those of Neanderthals (zmescience.com, gizmodo.com, scmp.com). The team recovered a Denisovan-linked collagen variant from two fossils with no surviving DNA. The Xujiayao collection includes 20 specimens excavated decades ago. The researchers argue that some Chinese fossils previously assigned to separate human groups may instead represent variation within the Denisovan lineage. That classification remains uncertain for specimens identified only by resemblance, and researchers say additional samples would help test it (zmescience.com, gizmodo.com). The team also compared Xujiayao anatomy with roughly 200 remains from other human groups to help distinguish Denisovan traits (gizmodo.com). Taxonomic debate: The Xujiayao fossils had been proposed as Homo juluensis, while the Harbin skull was classified as Homo longi; the new study argues that differences such as skull size may reflect variation within Denisovans rather than separate branches (zmescience.com). Geographic reach: Evidence places Denisovans from Siberia and the Tibetan Plateau to northeastern China and the Taiwan Strait, suggesting they occupied a wide range of Asian environments (zmescience.com). Reconstruction limits: Bones and molecular evidence cannot establish details such as skin tone or hairstyle, so lifelike portraits necessarily include artistic interpretation (zmescience.com).

items.title: [cbc.ca] Canadian police suspend use of Crime Stoppers after 1.5 million records exposed
items.content_html:
🎨 ✏️

Canadian police services are suspending their use of Crime Stoppers after a breach exposed more than 1.5 million tips submitted across Canada over 25 years, a CBC News investigation found. More than 850,000 records included personally identifiable information. The tips were managed through P3, software provided by U.S.-based Navigate360. Navigate360 acknowledged on Friday that its database had been breached between November 2025 and March 2026 and said potentially exposed information included names, addresses, birth dates and Social Security numbers. The company said it had no evidence the information had been used for fraud or identity theft. Police in several provinces have paused their use of the service while they assess the breach and its safeguards. Toronto and Ottawa police are directing people to report information through police channels, which do not necessarily offer the same anonymity. Crime Stoppers chapters and police are seeking further details from Navigate360. The company said it hired a cybersecurity firm to help strengthen security.

items.title: [thehackernews.com] PHP discloses third code-execution flaw as firewall patches remain pending
items.content_html:
🎨 ✏️

The PHP project disclosed a third, separate remote-code-execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-115560, in an advisory Friday, recommending that administrators disable session upload progress until a fix is available in a routine release. The warning follows emergency patches for PHP2Shell, two PHP flaws that can permit unauthenticated code execution. Those patches do not fix the new issue, which requires an unusual combination of session-serialization settings and application behavior that PHP considers unlikely in practice. Palo Alto Networks said Saturday that the PHP2Shell flaws also affect PAN-OS, its firewall operating system, and identified affected firewall and Panorama versions. The company said it was not aware of malicious exploitation against its products. Exposure is limited to management interfaces, and the company estimated that the first listed hotfixes would be available Oct. 26. Cybersecurity firm CYFIRMA separately reported suspected preparations by a Korean-speaking hacking group to exploit PHP2Shell against government and financial institutions in several countries. CYFIRMA assessed a possible link to North Korea’s Lazarus group with medium confidence but reported no confirmed successful intrusion.
